title: The Lovers: 124⁰ Sun Opposition Venus
excerpts: wetness is a loan word of mermaid gingiva.
bilateral heart, adrift on soft petroleum.
text:
can toothaches
                       send analog signals?

                                          roof of my mouth
                         unseparates raindrops:
                                        dressed the kiss with smog.

       lidocaine remains, however—
                       root canal has no signal.

          wetness is a loan word
    of mermaid gingiva.

     clench, scratch, snarl, eat;
           rational animal,
                  sluiced the unsweet.

           you cannot
           tongue-in-cheek out of this,
                                 go play leap-frog
               with a breath that bounces.

pattering pads—
     no, meat that matters.

            bilateral heart,
               adrift on *soft petroleum.*

text:

                         + medical clamp.

15:00: when the Almagest is about
matrilineal, *womb-sized* planets.

15:05: a cry pickled

15:15: diodes render blue

title: Mutya
excerpts: you are now meat simmered within mouths afraid to swallow.
the fleshed knot of worship and hunger.
text:
with the moistened jaw of Mut,
     we cherrypicked the barebones
                              of our dinner table.

         pitchforks baptized in sunset-fires
         rattle the carousel seats,
         horsemeat well-done swarms
         tonsils to teeth.
         lungs are hardened and shaped
         like *kakanin* enclosed within
         overripe banana leaves.

         lop the horses
         in digestible halves:
         **plating**.
         the rice picks
         the teeth apart:
         **plaything**.

         the ride treads merry in spurs—
         deadbeat horses, whirling
         unperturbed. you are now
         meat simmered within
         mouths afraid to swallow.
         rice dithers about the fall
         down the stomach, clinging
         to toothy carousels calcified
         against their will.

         ***who came first? womb, or God?***

         the dovetailing of mouth
         with both stomach and lungs:
         the fleshed knot of
         worship and hunger.
         here, you utter your first word:
         “Mama,” then you look at me.

         i wrap your overgrowth
         in the greenest
         banana leaves.

         Mut speaks through me:
         **“You are saved,**
         **for later.”**

title: For Etronie
excerpts:
i overripen:
sandpiper chorus out masts of throat,
open your hand and receive me.
text:
I am pouring ocean in urns.

Dollops dolled blue drop
onto their dewed lips, taut waterfalls.
My knees are sediment-bruised,
every sand-bathed speck flecks the skin
like pecks. I overripen:
sandpiper chorus out masts of throat,
the chittering dives their way down
to the bottom of the basin.
It was a giggle, t’was a laugh—
erupting like softened volcanoes.

Mildew, my friend of friends,
crop the worry-line out your brows
and listen to me.

The tide is lowered down
to palm-sized sheaths.
My hands are pruned thick
with sunsets by the sea.

I knead igneous rocks
into pebbles gentle.

Open your hand
and receive me.

title: Anagolay
excerpts: sampaguita strings link my teeth, together, gurgling mysteries in oil spills.
making way for August rain.
text:
I would like to clear the water,
            free it of fickle basilisks.

           The columbines brittle well
    into the twining dust of July,
and you've fettered me
          to the purpling skin
                     of your knees.

      We sat by *Baclaran’s* little pulpit
                     and opened our palms
                       to receive lizard alms.

      The pale brown scales swathed
    the skin of our hands;

   *sampaguita* strings link

                                 my teeth, together,

               gurgling mysteries
               in oil spills.

In communion spittle,
    the disjointed altar orbits.

    I am two *luwalhati* beads away
    from embedding pruned fingers
                                  into grotto ponds.

    Lizards scorn
                     the soles of their feet
                             as their grip slips
    from the unchurched ceiling,

        making way
               for August rain.

title: how many grams of protein are in the tears of my father's shirt?
excerpts: refining the posture of my fingertips, so they look less like my mother’s.
he dilutes—my mother’s hands.
columns:
If coconuts could talk,
they would slam their shells together
and spoil the lisp of their milk.

Abaca spells out
my name from between the fiber,
muted into spittle currencies.

My father’s shirt washes my hands,
refining the posture of my fingertips,
so they look less like my mother’s.

I comb the hairs from the coconut
in aims of matting the ends down.
Fingers turned fiberglass—

Oversand the coconut’s pores
before pouring spoiled fruit-milk
into abaca baskets.

My hands, woven into the abaca,
disappearing with folded knit—
I am acceptable now.

My father's shirt clears the dirt
from my nails, even with holes.
He dilutes—my mother’s hands.

The marketplace is open.
It is 7 in the morning—
even my mother is acceptable now.

title: Sinners
excerpts: born again as a Venus, unbecoming.
their gaze, poised, to architecture.
text:
I.
Tomorrow, we will exchange hands;
dousing fairy-catching fires before
coming to church. You cannot soak
yourself in Ash Wednesday residue.
You uncurl the other cheek
with a quivered lip.

II.
A nymph skitters mildly across the room.
She falters, and denies the drink offered
by tongue-contained hiss.

Faulty Salome flecks the womb
with inward steps.
Born again as a Venus,
unbecoming,

Her heart is her mother’s, again.

III.
The tongue pushes out
the fat extruding from the other cheek.
It sags and sags, downed with mildew.
The body is a morose candle
dimly lighting the path up the tower.

IV.
Basilisks are tethered still
to cathedral slippages.

The water is now dewormed.

The drinks spill the womb-water.

We extract the bones from Venus
to tighten the shoes of the dancer.
Her feet are slipping still
‘til she is christened in fire, again.

V.
Hands were exchanged today.
The fairies are godmothers
to Christ-borns.

The foreheads are emulsified
with ashy tinctures of water.

Our eyes abstain
from the lizards.

Their gaze, poised,
to architecture.

title: Bambanti
excerpts: little brown bodies strawmanned into furniture.
the crows overhead embroil the insular bambanti, who remained slack-jawed despite it all.
text:
i fluff a hungry crow’s feathers
to soften the blow.
slowly, he flies away.
i find his sun-baked carcass
on our side of the road.

the farmer passes his straw hat
around for a kilo of rice,
or perhaps a centavo or two.
hands dipped in arid soil,
with ounces of neither nickel
nor silver. he hitches jeeps and
buses bound south,
he walks back home,
slippery-palmed.

there were no faces
in the trike terminal today.
the driver wipes his forehead,
a headcount of yesterday’s coins.
he envisions 6-year old bellies
flattened to tabletops,
little brown bodies
strawmanned into furniture.
he spends the night
at the terminal once again.

i saw a mob of heads
down the streets, bumping
and drilling against each other.
an old man shrivels beneath
everyone else's knees.
his wails weighed down
by other grain-dead stomachs,
blued cheeks echoing the color
of abaca fiber they can't afford.

the noontime stillness
of the copper field
is damp with sweat, dankness.
the crows overhead embroil
the insular bambanti,
who remained slack-jawed
despite it all.

title: April Showers are Small, Diminutive
excerpts: mercy-tongues slippery enough for San Antonio’s shower blessing.
acid rain is also holy water at some point in sinner physics.
text:
When the sun patters alongside scattered forecasts
of rain, I inhabit the frogginess of it through
mercy-tongues slippery enough for San Antonio’s
shower blessing. Quiapo is candlelit with scores
of scorches, with acidic rain brittling
into slivering white onto the silver handlebars.
The flames play leap-frog with raindrops across shops.
I press against devotee chests and prayer quivers
through throats. Acid rain is also holy water at some point
in sinner physics. That I am: city-pest, run-on prayer,
San Antonio proxy. I inhabit the pronged state of frogs.
The riveting *ribbiting* distorts my graceless remarks.

title: i am a child i am a child i am a child
excerpts: clock hands are proboscis.
hollowing cheeks carving forbidden fruit. i am the paradise ghost.
text:
clock hands are proboscis. folded white skin like seashells; feeling sandpaper and hearing seagulls. a grin that stretches beyond the edge of your eyes; cheeks hurting, swelling like fresh apples. hoping noon was longer than it should be. a snake in the tree. paradise hanging like a ghost. now walking on sand, only sand. wishing the sun was gone.

—

clock hands drink from my fingers. each birthday invite houseflies that bear the faces of people i knew. wingfolds were smiles that fell like freshly cut nails. fingers offered to strangers who had once carved themselves seats in the party of my mind. they have rounded bellies and their hands are full. my ribs jut out of my skin. i give thanks with them. they try to smile.

clock hands touch the shape of my skull and tell it promises. i fit my eyes inside every dead animal; i wonder what it’s like. dry throat carrying only the spine of an apple. epidermis thinning each step forward to tomorrow. seeing ribs puncturing the sand. hanging on to heartbeats. i am alive. i am alive.

—

clock hands draw wrinkles on my forehead and laughs. birthday suit does not reach my wrists and ankles anymore—i am younger than ever. pushing nails down to fingers and fixing postures each second. avoiding mirrors and putting faces of children on house guests. they have party hats for heads and we do little dances and sing to ourselves: we are not yet dead.

—

clock hands point me towards north. my shoulders rise higher than my head. a bob in my throat shaped like the weight of regret. bones become skin. sand swallowing my footprints. north is where? the sun had never moved; eternal noon. hollowing cheeks carving forbidden fruit. i am the paradise ghost.

—

clock hands hold my face in wait. folds pile across my skin until i am thinned to bones. grinning yet it’s never whole. grumbling from my stomach mistaken for my throat. gnawing ache in knowing you can never dance like you did before. i own nothing, except a gaping hole i have stitched in me called life. it is never filled; the seats are empty and i drop like a fly.

title: god(girl)hood, and the things that help me sleep
excerpts: i want to be buried without your name falling from my lips because it would mean that you were big enough to be a truth i died for.
i will love you enough to make you unholy.
text:
i.

the sun pulverizes the night into fine powders and smoke, so
much so that the moon hangs its wounds in speckles of light
through the haze of it all in hopes those who need to see it will
do.

ii.

millennia-old dragon wounds inspiring poetry and downcast
gazes following the trail of turquoise blood. there is a little girl
in me whose fingertips are blue and she prays with black-tipped
matchsticks,
                   stolen coins, eyelashes, incense dust,
                   the space allowed between palms,
she found on the dejected sides of holy places. you could hear
the misremembered mantras from the quiver of her voice. she
is five years old and already knew there is something larger
than the wiry frame she’s born in.

already, she knew how to
bend her knees and beg for it.

iii.

you’d make mythologies out of anything,
                                                       anything to help you
                                                                                      escape.

in the darkness, i can forget about things bigger than me. in the
darkness, the shooting stars go nowhere. in the darkness, the
smoke holds no promises of castles in the sky or veiled fox
brides between bamboos. in the darkness, there is no dialogue
between mountaintops. in the darkness, i am no wanting
creature. in the darkness, there are no teeth marks in the hand
that feeds. in the darkness, there is no need to save me—
no need to save me.

i am allowed
hold my breath below the water
                                                                                   this time.

iv.

make an abyss out of what’s between my ribs and throw your
name into it. i will shake with every syllable like wind-stirred
candlelight. i will know what revelation feels like and why
there is so much to fear in love.

have you ever loved with a violence?
is it possible to love without it?

v.

the heart wants what it wants and it wants what it isn’t.
there is little difference between devotion and desperation; it’s
meted out by how much blasphemy these sordid, wanting
mouths would allow between their teeth. i grapple with the fact
that faith was inevitable before it was necessary and how
there’s always something to hold on to;
                                                           to aspire to want.
i want to be buried without your name falling from my lips
because it would mean that you were big enough to be a truth
i died for. if it is sacrilege, let it be. leave the wounds bleeding
and let the sinners come to it thinking they’d be forgiven if they
swipe their tongues against it. i swear i will love you enough to
make you unholy. i know you’d love to see me try. until then
i won’t apologize for anything
                                                 until i’m able to say goodnight.
